key_insight: Linear resolvent analysis of the mean stenotic flow reveals low-rank coherent structures that explain transitional dynamics, with axisymmetric shear-layer fluctuations dominating key post-stenotic stress responses.
engineering_relevance: This provides a reduced-order route to predict turbulent kinetic energy and turbulent wall shear stress in stenosis, supporting cardiovascular risk assessment from mean-flow data.
method: Compute the mean field from LES at Re=4000.
Use global linear stability and resolvent analysis to identify amplified coherent modes.
Reconstruct TKE and tWSS from the leading resolvent response mode and compare with SPOD.
evidence_signal: The model was validated against SPOD, showing strong alignment of the optimal resolvent response with the leading SPOD mode and successful reconstruction of TKE and tWSS.
watch_item: The approach is built on a mean-flow linearization at a specific Reynolds number, so transferability to other geometries, flow rates, or highly nonlinear regimes may be limited.
paper_title: Coherent structures modeling in stenotic transitional flow via resolvent analysis
